No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

The fort was built under Humayun and Sher Shah Suri. Excavations inside it since the 1950s have found settlement going back more than two thousand years. The walk covers the walls, gateways and mosque, and what each excavation revealed.

The date, start time, pace and language are arranged to suit your group.

What it covers

  • The three gateways and the walls of the sixteenth-century fort
  • The Qila-i-Kuhna mosque and the Sher Mandal
  • The excavations from the 1950s to the most recent seasons, and what each layer held
  • How archaeologists date a site lived on for more than two thousand years

How the time is spent

  1. Fort gateway 25 min

    Separate fort phases and literary associations.

    You: annotate evidence chart

  2. Bara Darwaza and walls 40 min

    Describe gateway construction and defensive design.

    You: sketch plan

  3. Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque 40 min

    Identify Sur-period architectural features from open areas.

    You: spot decorative features

  4. Sher Mandal and excavations interpretation 25 min

    Distinguish accessible monuments from reported excavations.

    You: debate evidence vs legend

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Identify and interpret key features of Purana Qila using material evidence and a site map.
  • Compare fort architecture, excavated occupation and contested identifications.
  • Distinguish directly visible fabric from reconstructed or debated historical claims.

You take away

Your annotated field card, sketches and notes.
